messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] RHIPE in Production Hadoop Jobs (enterprise usage) as compared to RMR
parts:
My question, is RHIPE being used in production in enterprises for running R jobs? 


Yes.
 
If so, how does it handle interfacing with the JVM on memory management for R?   Trying to manage R memory outside the JVM is a pain. 

From our mapred-xml

<property>
    <name>mapred.map.child.ulimit</name>
    <value>2310144</value>
and

 <property>
    <name>mapred.reduce.child.ulimit</name>
    <value>2310144</value>

This works for us. Assuming one is not doing something on a matrix or R object that is more than 1.5GB ...

parts:
So, as far as i know, ProcessBuilder (the code that launches new processes) is based on fork/exec.
The fork will need the same heapspace that the JVM started but the exec ought to release it.
So there could be a brief spike upon process creation, which happens once per map task.
So if one uses fileinputformat, keep the blocksizes large e.g. 128MB



On Wed, Apr 17, 2013 at 4:24 AM, Krishnaraj Gharpure <kagha...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Fishtank,

Going by your response below, (the mapred.map/reduce.child.ulimit parameter) would I be correct in saying that in using RHIPE jobs, R is internally spawned as a child process of the JVM, such that a copy of the JVM heap is replicated for the child process as well?

The reason I ask is because I was wondering if, in comparison, making calls to R directly in the Java MR job using JRI would prevent the spawning of child processes such that the R engine is spawned entirely _within_ the JVM, making memory management that much easier/predictable/controllable?

Thanks,

Krish.
